model: ATL800 / ATL900 automatic transfer switch controllers
applies_to: ATL800 and ATL900 ATS controllers (document I463 GB I 11 21); LINE3, BRK3 and TB2 items are ATL900 only.
summary: The ATL800 and ATL900 are Lovato's automatic transfer switch controllers for two (ATL800) or three (ATL900) sources. They talk Modbus RTU, ASCII and TCP through the optical port and EXP expansion modules. This map covers line voltages, frequencies, currents and powers, operating-time and operation counters, alarm and status words, and the mode, breaker and generator commands.

addressing.note: The tables print hex addresses (for example 3Ah) and the document says to send one less. Its read example asks for 3Ah with start address 00 39, and its write example sends 2F03h as 2F02h. 'address' here is already reduced by one.

source.title: ATL800 - ATL900 Automatic transfer switch controller - Communication protocol Modbus
source.pages: p. 2 (functions, example), p. 6 (Table 2), pp. 8-12 (measures, status, commands), p. 14 (write example)

notes: Word order: the read example returns 00 00 00 0A for a count of 10, so the high word comes first (ABCD).
Units as printed: line voltages are whole volts, frequency Hz/10, battery VDC/10, currents A/10000, powers kW, kvar and kVA /10000, power factor /10000.

Alarm bits at 9Ah (32-bit): bit 0 A01 battery voltage low, 1 A02 battery high, 2 A03 BRK1 timeout, 3 A04 BRK2 timeout, 4 A05 BRK3 timeout, 5-7 A06-A08 phase sequence lines 1-3, 8 A09 load not powered timeout, 9 A10 local battery charger, 10-12 A11-A13 genset battery chargers, 13 A14 emergency, 14-16 A15-A17 breaker trips, 17-19 A18-A20 breakers withdrawn, 20-22 A21-A23 genset not available, 23-25 A24-A26 maintenance hours, 26-28 A27-A29 maintenance operations, 29 A30 auxiliary voltage breaker, 30 A31 non-priority load breaker timeout, 31 A32 TB1 timeout. At 9Ch: bits 0-6 A33-A39 (tie and non-priority breakers), bits 7-14 user alarms UA1-UA8.

Left out: maintenance hours and operations-to-maintenance (units differ between lines), minimum/maximum battery voltage (unit printed as V while the live value is VDC/10), generic counters and analog I/O (user-defined units), digital I/O bit words, display-message and LED words, the 32-bit device global status at 2210h, remote variables, key simulation, and the setup parameters.
LINE2 status words are printed at 2176h/2177h while LINE1 is at 2074h/2075h; they are listed exactly as printed.
Input function status is left out: Table 3 lists it at 2078h, but the bit table for it says to read address 2178h, so the address is not settled.

integration.summary: Read 32-bit measures with function 04 at the table address minus one, high word first. 207Ch gives the mode and global alarm; write 2F00h (sent as 0x2EFF) to change mode, and 1C00h to open or close breakers.
integration.enable: Configure the port in setup menu M10 (node address P10.n.01, speed P10.n.02, data format P10.n.03, stop bits P10.n.04, protocol P10.n.05; IP settings for EXP1013).
quirks: Every address, read or write, is sent one lower than printed.
setup: Up to three communication ports (n = 1-3) can be set in menu M10.
Defaults: node 01, 9600 baud, 8 bits no parity, 1 stop bit, Modbus-RTU; Ethernet (EXP1013) default IP 192.168.1.1, IP port 1001.
gotchas: Line voltages are whole volts (no decimals).
The default Modbus TCP port is 1001, not 502.
